newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - KLM profit tumbles as Northwest crutch falls.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - KLM profit tumbles as Northwest crutch falls.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM Royal Dutch Airlines tumbled into the red in the third quarter as operating expenses mushroomed and equity revaluations fell away.

A 40 percent higher fuel bill coupled with increased wage costs pushed KLM into a third-quarter operating loss of 19 million guilders ($10.3 million), along with higher landing, air navigation and third party handling charges.
This compares with an operating profit of 56 million guilders a year earlier.

With no further revaluations of KLM's holding in U.S. partner Northwest Airlines to beef up the bottom line, it also reported a third quarter net loss of seven million guilders, down from a 102 million profit the previous year.
The results cut nine month net profits to 522 million or 5.62 guilders per share, down from 539 million in the year-ago period.
In previous quarters, a steady decline in KLM's operating profits was masked by the revaluation of its equity stake in Northwest. But this process was completed in the first half of 1996-97.
Northwest's contribution this quarter dwindled to just three million guilders from 131 million in the previous quarter.
KLM said it was optimistic that its ambitious three-year Focus 2000 restructuring programme would reach its target of boosting annual operating revenues.
"The assessments so far confirm the possibility to structurally improve operating income by 1.5 billion guilders over a three-year period," it said.

Projects already being implemented in passenger sales include electronic shopping and the introduction of a new sales and distribution approach. Information technology would optimise capacity use at its cargo division, KLM said.

But industry observers are sceptical, pointing to union reluctance to cooperate on further cutbacks and Tuesday's decision by Dutch travel agents to take KLM to court over its unilateral decision to cut commission on tickets.
"Pilots, for example, are absolutely not prepared to take a (pay) cut," one analyst said.
KLM said it was maintaining its earlier forecast that full-year 1996-97 net profit before restructuring charges would be about 150 million guilders lower than the previous year's record 547 million.
Contrary to most analysts' expectations, the airline said it would not be booking its 18.8 percent share of Northwest profits in its final quarter.
"The forecast net result for the fourth quarter contains no result from KLM's stake in Northwest Airlines," it said.
"(This) seems a little strange," said Bert van Hoogenhuyze, airlines analyst with brokers Amstgeld.
The airline had been unable to book its share of Northwest earnings as the U.S. carrier had negative shareholders' equity, but this returned to the black in December.
KLM spokesman Hans Leijte said the Dutch carrier had not officially been notified of Northwest's return to positive shareholders' equity.
"KLM has repeatedly stated that it expected to book its share of Northwest profits during the course of 1997...we did not say when," he said.

The carrier's reluctance to inflate its bottom line with Northwest profits in the fourth quarter could be aimed at chivying unions into agreeing far-reaching cuts, said one analyst who declined to be named.
KLM shares were down one guilder at 53.50 guilders within minutes of the results being released, but had rallied 10 cents to 53.60 by 1420 GMT.

At this price they are trading just above their current book value of 50 guilders per share, but both book value and earnings per share are set to increase when last December's share buy-back deal takes effect.
Under the 976 million guilder deal, due to be approved by an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on March 3, KLM will buy back from the Dutch state and withdraw more than 17 million common shares.

Had the transaction become effective this quarter, pro forma net income per common share for the nine-month period to end-December would have been 6.85 guilders rather than the current 5.62 guilders, KLM said.
Once approved, the deal will be included in KLM's balance sheet as of March 31 this year, it added. ($ = 1.844 Dutch Guilders)
